newsitem.title: CHINA: China rejects Patten criticism on Hong Kong laws.
newsitem.headline: China rejects Patten criticism on Hong Kong laws.

text.p: China on Tuesday rejected Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten's criticism of its proposal to abolish a series of laws in the territory after it reverts to Beijing control, saying it was China's internal affair.

"We cannot accept Patten's so-called statement," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said in reply to a reporter's question about criticism of plans to abolish laws on democratic elections and civil liberties after the transfer of power this year.
The spokesman also called on the Hong Kong government to avoid making statements that misled the public or undermined morale in the territory which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Patten had condemned a move by the China-appointed panel known as the Preparatory Committee to draw up a list of 25 laws and articles for repeal or amendment after the transfer of power.
Shen said the Preparatory Committee had the authority to review existing Hong Kong laws to determine whether they were in conflict with the Basic Law, a mini-constitution drafted for the territory.
"This is entirely an internal matter for China," he said.
